display.purpose: The single landing headline. Not used inside the workspace.

body.purpose: Default size for nearly all UI text.

edgeCode.purpose: Machine-exact values only, formatted like a film negative's printed edge code: seed numbers, hex, character counts.

motion.name: tile-hover-scale
motion.purpose: The loupe-style hover cue on a Pick-stage grid tile — a slight zoom, as if a loupe were placed over the frame.

motion.name: color-transition
motion.purpose: Border/fill color change on hover and selection.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single primary action per stage — Generate, Regenerate, Continue, Export.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--primary, oklch(0.543 0.174 29.7)); color: #fff; padding: 6px 12px; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; border: none; border-radius: 3.2px; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.15s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: oklch(0.46 0.19 29.7); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--primary, oklch(0.543 0.174 29.7)); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: EdgeTag
components.description: Plain bracketed monospace tag for a fixed/locked value — replaces a lock icon with a literal label.
components.css: .ds-edge-tag { font-family: 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.02em; color: oklch(0.46 0.006 85); }

components.name: GreaseCircle selection mark
components.description: The system's one selection mark: two overlapping, slightly misaligned hand-drawn-feeling red rings over a chosen tile.
components.css: .ds-tile-wrap { position: relative; } .ds-tile-img { display: block; width: 100%; object-fit: cover; } .ds-grease-circle { position: absolute; inset: -7%; width: 114%; height: 114%; pointer-events: none; }

components.name: Selectable Tile (swatch/asset-type/bracket/image)
components.description: The reused choice pattern: square corners, solid frame border, red-wash fill when selected.
components.css: .ds-tile { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 4px; width: 76px; padding: 6px; border: 1px solid oklch(0.2 0.004 85 / 0.5); background: #fff; text-align: center; cursor: pointer; } .ds-tile:hover { background: oklch(0.955 0.004 90); } .ds-tile-selected { border-color: var(--primary, oklch(0.543 0.174 29.7)); background: oklch(0.543 0.174 29.7 / 0.05); } .ds-tile-preview { width: 32px; height: 32px; border: 1px solid oklch(0.2 0.004 85 / 0.5); background: linear-gradient(135deg, oklch(0.94 0.03 30), oklch(0.8 0.1 29)); } .ds-tile-label { font-size: 11px; line-height: 1.2; color: oklch(0.2 0.004 85); }

components.name: Wordmark
components.description: The app name folded into the bracket-tag vocabulary — replaces a generic sparkle/wand icon.
components.css: .ds-wordmark { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; color: oklch(0.2 0.004 85); } .ds-wordmark-bracket { font-family: 'Geist Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; color: var(--primary, oklch(0.543 0.174 29.7)); }

narrative.overview:
Brief Compiler is a physical production document being marked up by hand — the interface's central act, look at a grid of variations and circle the winner, gets the exact ritual it's already named after in photography. Every screen reads like something that could be stapled into a production binder: light-table white, ruled black frame-lines around every image like sprocket-adjacent negative strips, and one uncompromising grease-pencil red that means exactly one thing everywhere it appears — this is the mark, this is the action. Nothing is decorative; nothing performs trustworthiness with soft gradients or a sparkle icon. It earns trust the way a real contact sheet does, by being legible, exact, and consistent.

This replaced an earlier, unreviewed default: neutral grays, one soft indigo accent, bordered flat cards on a generic Tailwind/shadcn base, running underneath Atlaskit components still wearing unbranded Atlassian blue. That system was never chosen — it was the shape the framework defaults settle into when nobody picks a world. This one was chosen through Impeccable's direction round (seed 42e6fbdb): six catalog challengers were weighed and declined, and the user picked this direction — Impeccable's own top-ranked grounded candidate — over the assigned build candidate, re-roll, and the standing exit.
keyCharacteristics: One accent color, grease-pencil red, spent on primary actions and the literal hand-drawn "chosen" mark — never as decoration
Solid black 1px frame-lines around every image tile, not soft gray hairlines — sharp corners on frames and marks, barely-eased corners on interactive chrome only
A plain bracketed monospace tag, [FIXED] / [LOCKED], replaces a lock icon wherever a value never touches the model or won't change this regeneration
A hand-drawn grease-pencil circle is the system's one selection mark — used only where a human actually chose something
Atlaskit's own components are rebranded to the same red via its supported theming API, so Button/Lozenge/links/focus rings match the rest of the system
Dark mode is the same world lit differently: a darkroom safelight rather than a separate identity

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Grease-pencil red means exactly two things: a primary action, or a human's hand-drawn choice. It never fills a background, never decorates a badge at rest, and never appears twice for two different reasons on the same screen.

rules.name: The Frame vs. Border Rule
rules.body: border-frame (solid ink) is reserved for the edge of an image tile. border (translucent ink) is for everything else. Promoting an ordinary divider to border-frame is the tell that this system is being imitated rather than used.

rules.name: The Plain Label Rule
rules.body: A protected value gets the literal tag [FIXED] or [LOCKED] in Edge-code type, never a lock glyph standing alone.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: A box-shadow never indicates elevation, hover, or selection — those are a border/fill change or the grease-pencil mark.

rules.name: The Sharp Frame Rule
rules.body: Anything that holds a generated or reference image gets a square corner and a solid border-frame edge. Rounding an image tile is the fastest way this system starts looking like the generic app it replaced.

dos: Do keep grease-pencil red to primary actions and the GreaseCircle mark only (The One Red Rule).
Do use border-frame (solid) for image-tile edges and border (translucent) for everything else (The Frame vs. Border Rule).
Do brand every new Atlaskit surface through providers.tsx's theme options rather than letting a component default to Atlassian blue.
Do use [FIXED] / [LOCKED] (EdgeTag) only where the claim is literally true.
Do keep image tiles and swatch tiles square-cornered; keep interactive chrome barely-eased.
donts: Don't round an image or reference tile — that's the tell this system reverted to the generic default (The Sharp Frame Rule).
Don't introduce a second saturated accent; route anything that isn't the grease-pencil red through ink/paper/frame neutrals.
Don't add a box-shadow for elevation, hover, or selection state.
Don't apply GreaseCircle or EdgeTag decoratively — both mean something specific and lose their force the moment they're sprinkled for texture.
Don't leave a new Atlaskit component unbranded; check it picks up the red, not Atlassian blue, before shipping it.
